rows.title: A preliminary investigation of the relationship between rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and fear inhibition processes in the context of circadian misalignment.
rows.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
rows.verified_title: A preliminary investigation of the relationship between rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and fear inhibition processes in the context of circadian misalignment.
rows.verified_journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
rows.focus: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is implicated in fear inhibition processes critical for trauma recovery. However, prior experimental models of REM sleep disruption have lacked ecological validity by manipulating sleep without accounting for circadian timing. Circadian misalignment frequently occurs in occupations at high risk of trauma exposure. The present study examined the relationship between REM sleep and fear inhibition in the context of experimentally induced circadian misalignment. A total of 42 healthy adults (Mage = 24.89, SD = 5.11) were randomized to one of three conditions for four nights: (a) normal control (n = 18), (b) circadian disruption with placebo administration (n = 14), or (c) circadian disruption with melatonin (3 mg) administration (n = 10). Circadian disruption consisted of two consecutive 4-hr phase advances. Fear inhibition was measured via the fear-potentiated startle task. Degree of circadian misalignment was measured via the phase angle between peak urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin and scheduled wake time. Greater circadian misalignment on Night 4 significantly predicted larger reductions in both REM% (p = .010) and REM minutes (p = .002) that night. Controlling for changes in total sleep time and slow wave sleep, reductions in REM minutes on Night 4 significantly predicted poorer extinction recall the following day (ΔR² = .12, p = .040), whereas reductions in REM% showed a nonsignificant small-to-moderate association (p = .087). Individuals experiencing greater reductions in REM sleep under circadian misalignment demonstrated poorer extinction recall. Interestingly, circadian misalignment predicted the same change in sleep (reduced REM minutes) also linked to poor extinction recall. Given the role of extinction recall in trauma-related psychopathology, these findings may have implications for frontline personnel at increased risk for posttraumatic stress disorder. However, larger samples are needed to confirm these preliminary findings. (PsycInfo Database Record (c) 2026 APA, all rights reserved).

rows.title: Association Between Serum Trace Elements and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Multiple-Exposure Models.
rows.journal: Journal of preventive medicine and public health = Yebang Uihakhoe chi
rows.verified_title: Association Between Serum Trace Elements and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Multiple-Exposure Models.
rows.verified_journal: Journal of preventive medicine and public health = Yebang Uihakhoe chi
rows.focus: The association between trace elements and obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains an active area of research, and further studies are needed to clarify these relationships. This study examined correlations between serum essential trace element concentrations and polysomnography-confirmed OSA. This cross-sectional study included patients recruited from the Sleep Disorders Center of Farabi Hospital in western Iran. Participants were classified as patients with OSA (n = 54) or controls without OSA (n = 45). Iron (Fe) levels were significantly higher in participants with OSA than in controls (P = 0.04). Higher Fe levels were associated with greater odds of OSA (P for trend = 0.02). Participants in the fourth Fe quartile had higher odds of OSA than those in the lowest quartile, although this association was of borderline statistical significance (odds ratio [OR] = 3.00; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.96-10.00; P = 0.06). In contrast, participants in the second and third magnesium (Mg) quartiles had lower odds of OSA than those in the first quartile (Q2: OR = 0.31; 95% CI: 0.09-0.96; Q3: OR = 0.26; 95% CI: 0.07-0.82). In the generalized weighted quantile sum (GWQS) regression model, the association between the metal mixture and OSA was not statistically significant β= - 0.22, P = 0.59). Serum concentrations of selected micronutrients may be associated with OSA. The findings suggested a positive association between higher Fe concentrations and OSA, whereas intermediate Mg concentrations were associated with lower odds of OSA.

rows.title: Stability-enhanced liposomal system co-loaded with γ-aminobutyric acid and naringenin: outstanding sleep-promoting efficacy.
rows.journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
rows.verified_title: Stability-enhanced liposomal system co-loaded with γ-aminobutyric acid and naringenin: outstanding sleep-promoting efficacy.
rows.verified_journal: Journal of the science of food and agriculture
rows.focus: Due to weak stability and bioavailability, γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and naringenin (Nar), two agents with sleep-promoting activities, are limited in practical application. To improve their sleep-promoting efficacy, this study developed a stability-enhanced co-loaded liposomal system (GABA-Nar-Lip) as a lyophilized powder. The non-lyophilized GABA-Nar-Lip exhibited good dispersibility, with an average particle size of 161.34 ± 1.68 nm, and achieved encapsulation efficiencies of 46.18 ± 0.32% (GABA) and 82.01 ± 1.33% (Nar), respectively. The stability of GABA-Nar-Lip was significantly enhanced after lyophilization with sugars (especially 0.10 g mL-1 trehalose) as cryoprotectants (CPAs), and maintained targeted release in the small intestine. The CPAs exerted cryoprotective effects by replacing water molecules and forming hydrogen bonds with soy phosphatidylcholine, thereby preserving the spherical structure and unilamellar vesicle morphology of the liposomes. In caffeine-induced zebrafish models, lyophilized GABA-Nar-Lip showed an inferior but still significant effect in sleep latency reduction. Moreover, it decreased nocturnal twitching activity and enhanced daytime locomotor activity on the following day, without the adverse effects associated with melatonin, such as poor sleep quality and reduced daytime activity. The stabilized lyophilized GABA-Nar-Lip powder is a promising, safe sleep aid with balanced efficacy and no compromise to next-day performance, supporting its potential application in dietary sleep interventions. © 2026 Society of Chemical Industry.

rows.title: Differences in circadian rhythm changes between myopic and non-myopic college students over 2 years.
rows.verified_title: Differences in circadian rhythm changes between myopic and non-myopic college students over 2 years.
rows.focus: This study aimed to characterize and compare the differences in circadian rhythm changes during 2 years between college students with myopia and non-myopia based on a longitudinal cohort study. Wake-up time and bedtime were obtained through a self-administered questionnaire. Chronotype was assessed using the reduced Morningness-Eveningness Questionnaire (rMEQ). Circadian rhythm timing was determined by dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO), measured through hourly saliva collection from 21:00 to 01:00. A total of 450 college students (146 [32.4%] males) with a mean age of 18.65 ± 1.05 years were included, of whom 353 (78.4%) students had myopia. Compared with non-myopic individuals, myopic students slept later, woke up earlier, and exhibited lower rMEQ scores at baseline. Over the 2-year follow-up, both groups showed significantly earlier bedtimes, later wake-up times, and higher rMEQ scores. Only myopic students demonstrated a 45-minute delay in DLMO after the 2-year follow-up. After adjusting for potential confounders, linear mixed-effects models showed that myopic individuals had later bedtimes and earlier wake-up times. These findings indicate significant circadian rhythm changes in individuals with myopia, suggesting the potential of targeted sleep rhythm interventions on preventing myopia.

rows.title: Circadian and behavioral timing in MASLD: a systematic review of human observational studies.
rows.verified_title: Circadian and behavioral timing in MASLD: a systematic review of human observational studies.
rows.focus: Circadian disruption may affect metabolism through altered timing of sleep, activity, light exposure, hormonal rhythms, and food intake. However, its relationship with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), including fibrosis and cirrhosis remains unclear. To evaluate associations between circadian and behavioural timing exposures and MASLD in observational studies. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched from inception to 14 July 2026. Eligible studies examined naturally occurring timing-related exposures in adults and reported steatosis, fibrosis, cirrhosis, or quantitative liver-fat outcomes. Findings were synthesized narratively because heterogeneity precluded pooling. Risk of bias was assessed using AXIS or the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty using an adapted domain-level GRADE approach (PROSPERO Registration number: CRD420261381636). Twenty-four independent MASLD-related evidence sources were included in the primary synthesis; two additional mixed-aetiology cirrhosis studies were considered contextually. Shift work showed the most consistent associations and most longitudinal evidence. Chronotype was generally associated with disease occurrence but inconsistently with advanced outcomes: intermediate or late chronotype was associated with fibrosis in one clinical cohort, whereas morning chronotype was not independently associated with incident cirrhosis in a prospective cohort. Later sleep timing was associated with prevalent MASLD and, in one NHANES analysis, fibrosis. Evidence for objective rest-activity rhythms, light exposure, meal timing, and melatonin phase remained limited or heterogeneous. Mixed-aetiology cirrhosis studies suggested that advanced liver disease may itself disrupt circadian physiology. Circadian and behavioural timing exposures showed trends associated with MASLD-related outcomes, with the most consistent evidence for shift work. Residual confounding, cross-sectional designs, self-reported exposures, heterogeneous outcomes, and reverse causality preclude causal conclusions. Prospective studies using objective circadian phenotyping and standardized fibrosis outcomes are needed. This research did not receive any specific grant from funding agencies in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

rows.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruption in Alzheimer's Disease: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Therapeutic Approaches.
rows.verified_title: Circadian Rhythm Disruption in Alzheimer's Disease: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Therapeutic Approaches.
rows.focus: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurological disorder characterized by unusual behavior, memory deterioration, and a decline in cognitive abilities. A growing body of research indicates that circadian rhythm disturbances play a crucial role in the pathophysiology of AD, impacting both molecular processes and clinical outcomes. This review critically evaluates the molecular interplay between circadian rhythm disruption and AD pathology, explores its impact on clinical manifestations and disease progression, and assesses emerging diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to restore circadian regulation and improve patient outcomes. A thorough analysis of recent research on molecular clock genes (CLOCK, BMAL1, PER, and CRY) and their roles in regulating hormone rhythms, metabolism, and sleep-wake cycles was conducted. Research on technology-based methods, therapeutic treatments, and circadian biomarkers was assessed to determine their applicability in AD. Circadian gene dysregulation was found to exacerbate tau hyperphosphorylation, amyloid- β accumulation, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation. Clinically, circadian disruption manifests itself as mood disorders, sleep-wake abnormalities, and accelerated cognitive deterioration. Light therapy, melatonin supplements, chrono-pharmacology, and behavioural techniques are among the interventions that have shown promise in restoring rhythm stability. Wearables, smart lighting, neuromodulation, and multi-omics modelling are examples of technological advancements that increase the range of diagnostic and treatment possibilities. Patient heterogeneity, translational gaps, and a lack of mechanistic knowledge continue to pose difficulties despite progress. To enhance AD outcomes, future research should focus on integrated, customized therapies that target the circadian rhythm.

rows.title: Smartphone-based digital phenotyping of sighted non-24-h sleep-wake disorder: A 258-d continuous circadian monitoring study.
rows.verified_title: Smartphone-based digital phenotyping of sighted non-24-h sleep-wake disorder: A 258-d continuous circadian monitoring study.
rows.focus: Diagnosing Non-24-h Sleep-Wake Disorder (N24SWD) in sighted individuals remains difficult due to the need for long-term, high-resolution monitoring of circadian rhythms. While actigraphy and dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO) are considered gold standards, their extended use is often impractical and compliance-intensive. We present a 258-d continuous assessment using smartphone-based digital phenotyping, which unobtrusively inferred sleep-wake patterns from passive smartphone interaction data using the app-count algorithm and Tudor-Locke rules. Specifically, the Rhythm app passively logged time-stamped human-smartphone interaction events-screen on/off, notifications, and the application in use-rather than accelerometry, aggregated into non-overlapping 5-min epochs scored as sleep or wake by the absence or presence of interaction. Results were validated against 109 d of actigraphy and 7 d of dynamic DLMO sampling, showing strong concordance. Because this metric reflected human-smartphone interaction rather than a second accelerometer stream, the nearly identical circadian periods from smartphone (25.16 h) and actigraphy (25.11 h) indicate that interaction-based phenotyping can independently recover the long-term free-running period. Smartphone-based tracking offers a practical, low-burden alternative for long-term circadian monitoring in N24SWD.

rows.title: Effects of daytime versus nighttime feeding on nutrient digestion, blood biochemical parameters, gastrointestinal microbiota, and metabolites in sheep.
rows.verified_title: Effects of daytime versus nighttime feeding on nutrient digestion, blood biochemical parameters, gastrointestinal microbiota, and metabolites in sheep.
rows.focus: Feeding time is a modifiable management factor that regulates nutrient digestibility and circadian physiological rhythms in ruminants. Twelve 7-month-old Dorper × Hu crossbred rams with an initial body weight of 47 ± 2.42 kg were individually housed in metabolism crates and randomly allocated to two feeding groups provided with an identical basal diet: daytime feeding (DP, feed available 08:00-20:00, n = 6) and nighttime feeding (NP, feed available 20:00-08:00, n = 6). Each ram served as the experimental unit. After a 7-day adaptation, feces and urine were collected for 7 days by total collection. Blood was sampled over 4 consecutive days, and ruminal, cecal, and longissimus dorsi samples were collected after slaughter. Non-omics outcomes were analyzed using Student's t-test; microbial relative abundances were compared using Welch's t-tests, and community-level differences were evaluated using analysis of similarities and permutational multivariate analysis of variance. Differential metabolites were identified using a variable importance in projection value > 1 and Student's t-test at P < 0.05. Descriptive co-variation patterns between differential microbiota and metabolites were visualized via Spearman's rank correlation. Ether extract digestibility (P = 0.012), nitrogen digestibility (P = 0.041), and plasma urea concentration (P = 0.011) were greater in DP than NP sheep. Concentrations of malondialdehyde, total antioxidant capacity, interferon-γ, interleukin-10, tumor necrosis factor-α, glucagon-like peptide-1, serotonin, and melatonin were greater in NP sheep (P ≤ 0.017). Feeding schedule was also associated with different ruminal and cecal microbial taxa and metabolite profiles. Carcass traits and physical meat quality did not differ between treatments. Thus, feeding time markedly remodeled nutrient digestibility, circulating biomarkers, and gastrointestinal profiles, but longer trials are required to determine effects on growth performance and feed efficiency.

rows.title: Structure-Switching Aptamer-Based Molecular Pendulum for Profiling Melatonin Circadian Dynamics in Humans.
rows.verified_title: Structure-Switching Aptamer-Based Molecular Pendulum for Profiling Melatonin Circadian Dynamics in Humans.
rows.focus: Continuous electrochemical monitoring of small molecules remains difficult due to their small size and lack of enzymatic sensing strategies. Here, we develop a structure-switching aptamer molecular pendulum platform for reagentless electrochemical detection of small molecules, including melatonin and cortisol. Target binding induces a conformational change in the receptor, which increases the hydrodynamic diameter of the construct, thereby slowing electron transfer kinetics and resulting in a measurable time-resolved electrochemical current. To explore the feasibility of melatonin sensing in vivo, we validated the presence and circadian dynamics of melatonin in human interstitial fluid using mass spectrometry. We then demonstrated quantitative electrochemical detection of melatonin directly in human ISF, with signals that mirror the circadian profile observed by mass spectrometry. This work provides a foundation for continuous, minimally invasive monitoring of circadian biomarkers using electrochemical sensors.
